clue.text: A novel spot in Devon

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the 1855 adventure novel by Charles Kingsley
second meaning: the seaside village in Devon, England, named after that book

explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England; the village took its name, exclamation mark and all, from Kingsley's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The same name belongs both to a Victorian book by Kingsley and to a resort village on the north Devon coast.

clue.text: Insect that nests with snake

parts.note: W is a standard abbreviation for with
the asp is a venomous Egyptian snake

explanation.surface: An insect sharing its nest with a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: This stinging yellow-and-black insect builds papery nests, so it is an insect that nests.

clue.text: Bound to leave something out

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a light jump or hop
second meaning: to omit or pass over

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' reads as 'certain to', but the clue splits after Bound.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a small springing jump and a verb for passing over or omitting part of something.

clue.text: A complaint that makes Scots lawyer go quiet

parts.note: in Scotland a solicitor is a Writer, as in Writer to the Signet
scram is slang for go away
p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: An ailment that silences a Scottish lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: Writer is the old Scottish word for a solicitor; the apostrophe is added to the joined letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This painful hand spasm brought on by long spells of handwriting is a medical complaint or ailment.

clue.text: One who regrets accepting twenty shillings — a sovereign

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: one who rues something
twenty shillings made a pound, abbreviated L from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: A monarch counting the cost of taking a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1971 the British pound was divided into twenty shillings; a sovereign was also a pound coin, which sharpens the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign is a monarch, a king or queen who governs a country.

clue.text: Careful management makes old man really heartless

parts.note: old man is informal for a husband

indicators.note: with its heart gone a word keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of really

explanation.surface: A cold, unfeeling old husband who manages money carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means thrifty, economical handling of resources, as well as farming crops and animals.

clue.text: The Church' incomplete as address for a priest

indicators.note: incomplete means the word is missing its final letter

parts.note: an abbey is a great church, as in the Abbey for Westminster Abbey

explanation.surface: A church left unfinished, and how to address its priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbé is the French title used when speaking to or of a priest or cleric.

clue.text: Brought to a satisfactory conclusion, saying little

definitions.meaning: first meaning: settled, wrapped up, all sorted

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one quiet negotiator; the clue splits at the comma.
explanation.definitionFit: A deal fastened up is finished successfully, and a person fastened up is reticent and uncommunicative.

clue.text: English doctor, ancient chap, given more courage

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree
olden means of former times
Ed is a man's name, a typical chap

explanation.surface: An English doctor and an old fellow find fresh courage.
explanation.definitionFit: To be made bolder is to be encouraged, with confidence or nerve increased.

clue.text: A shade not as blue

parts.note: a shade is a ghost or spirit
less means not as much

explanation.surface: Looks like comparing colours: one shade paler than blue.
explanation.walkthrough: Shade and blue both suggest colour; here a shade is a ghost and blue means sad.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue means low and dejected, lacking energy or liveliness, which is being without spirit.

clue.text: Cut nuts back

indicators.note: back means the word is read from right to left

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: Trimming back some nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: A knife thrust that wounds is a stab, and a cut is a similar wound from a blade.

clue.text: Manage to conceal it isn't a dream

indicators.note: to conceal a phrase is to disguise it, here by jumbling its letters

parts.note: the letters of the phrase, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone managing to hide that life isn't a dream.
explanation.definitionFit: To administrate is to run, direct or oversee affairs, a synonym of manage.

clue.text: Fifty thousand are wrong, completely

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fifty thousand people all mistaken, utterly.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something heart and soul is an idiom for doing it wholeheartedly, with total commitment.

clue.text: Tom's saddened by rejection

parts.note: Tom Thumb is the tiny hero of the folk tale, so Tom's is Thumb's
down means low in spirits

explanation.surface: Tom is upset at being turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Thumb's apostrophe-s supplies the plural ending of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A downward-pointing gesture with the hand signals disapproval, so the phrase means refusal or rejection.

clue.text: Call up — call outside the state is free

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to call something is to name it

indicators.note: outside means one word wraps around the other

parts.note: to cite is to summon or call to court
PA is the abbreviation for Pennsylvania

explanation.surface: A call-up from the state promising freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: Call appears twice with two different jobs; the state is a US state here, not the government.
explanation.definitionFit: To emancipate is to free from slavery or restriction, here as a verb meaning to liberate.

clue.text: Made those changes to estate

indicators.note: changes tells us to alter the order of these letters

parts.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: Someone altered a country estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A homestead is a farmhouse with its land and outbuildings, a small rural estate.

clue.text: Rose appearing in elegant variety

indicators.note: a variety is a different version, so the letters take another form

parts.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: A rose showing up in a handsome cultivated variety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in elegant variety' looks like gardening talk; 'in' is part of the fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is the sweetbriar, a wild European rose with fragrant leaves.

clue.text: One dried up river

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
sere means withered and dry

explanation.surface: A river that has run dry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isère is a tributary of the Rhône flowing through south-east France.

clue.text: A way of speaking of a police district

indicators.note: speaking means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a manner is a way of doing something; in non-rhotic British speech the two words sound alike

explanation.surface: Looks like it asks for a dialect of some police area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A way of speaking' looks like a single phrase meaning accent; the clue splits it.
explanation.definitionFit: In British police slang an officer's manor is the patch or district they work in.

clue.text: Artist's model, someone of no importance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a jointed wooden dummy used by painters
second meaning: a nonentity, a person used as a mere puppet

explanation.walkthrough: An artist's model sounds like a person sitting for a portrait; here it is a mannequin.
explanation.definitionFit: The mannequin painters pose for drapery is called this, and by extension a person with no real influence.

clue.text: Civic amenity often provided by dizzy city

parts.note: a swimming head is a dizzy one
Bath is a city in Somerset, England

explanation.surface: A council laying on local facilities in a giddy town.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is an English spa city famous for its Roman baths.
explanation.definitionFit: A public pool for swimming is a typical leisure facility a town council supplies for residents.

clue.text: Opinion about, say, father

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: my bet is that means my opinion is that
e.g. means for example, which is what say means here

explanation.surface: Someone's view on, for instance, their dad.
explanation.definitionFit: To father a child is to beget it, a verb meaning to sire or procreate.

clue.text: Starts to serve time in Russian prison

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their initial letters

parts.note: the initial letters of four words

explanation.surface: Beginning a sentence in a Russian jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is old slang for prison, as in doing time in stir.

clue.text: Stern teller of tales to an audience.

indicators.note: to an audience means as heard by listeners

parts.note: the Brothers Grimm collected German fairy tales

explanation.surface: A severe storyteller reading aloud to listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: Grim means forbidding and severe, as stern does, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Lady love first to say yes

indicators.note: first places the letter for love at the front, ahead of the name

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, shaped like the letter O
Kay is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman's beloved is the first to accept a proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: To okay something is to approve or give it the go-ahead, the verb for saying yes.

clue.text: Pole invested with double MC

indicators.note: to be invested with something is to be clothed in it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a ringer is a person's exact lookalike
a mast is a tall pole

explanation.surface: A Polish man given double master-of-ceremonies duties.
explanation.walkthrough: Pole looks like a nationality; it is the post.
explanation.definitionFit: The ringmaster introduces the acts at a circus, acting as its master of ceremonies.

clue.text: Trotsky came back for the festival

indicators.note: coming back means the name is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Leon Trotsky was the Russian revolutionary

explanation.surface: Trotsky returning home for the holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is another name for Christmas, the winter festival, from the French word.

clue.text: Part of the band decided not to start, with fog about outside.

indicators.note: outside means wrapping around the rest
about means turned round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: murk is thick gloom or fog

indicators.note: not to start means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a decided matter is settled

explanation.surface: A band member who decided not to begin in the fog.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed fog splits around the shortened word, its first letter in front and the rest behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A kettledrum, or timpani, is a large copper drum played in an orchestra, so one part of it.
